title: stream-duration-discount-framework-and-contract-templates
author: Leah Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: Define a standardized pricing framework and contract templates for duration-based discounts on long-running streaming and session-oriented inference workloads. This doc codifies eligibility, discount tiers, contract language, billing hooks, telemetry requirements, and a rollout/playbook for sales, finance, and customer success.

Background

Redwood has observed two commercial patterns where duration-sensitive discounts are necessary: (1) customers with sustained, predictable streaming sessions (e.g., call transcription, conversational agents with long sessions) and (2) high-throughput background ingestion pipelines that keep a small number of long-lived connections to the runtime. Current per-token pricing underestimates the economic benefit of reserving capacity and amortizing KV-cache and batching gains across long sessions. This framework provides clear, auditable rules for offering discounts while protecting unit economics.

Goals

- Make discounting predictable and automatable for sales and finance.
- Tie discounts to measurable signals (session duration, average active connections, KV cache hit, and run-time occupancy).
- Ensure discounts preserve SLO alignment and avoid gaming.
- Provide readily usable legal language and billing hook implementations for engineering.

Discount framework summary

Key concepts:

- Session duration (SD): wall-clock time an active session is maintained (in minutes).
- Discount window: the period for which we evaluate SD (rolling 30 days).
- Stability signal: percentage of sessions that exceed a customer-defined threshold.

Eligibility rules (must all be satisfied):

1) Account-level opt-in to duration program (sales checkbox / contract clause).
2) Median SD over a 30-day window >= 15 minutes.
3) At least 500 sessions (or equivalent 7-day sustained concurrently active minutes > 20k) in the evaluation window.
4) No significant QoS regressions during the previous 90 days (SLO breach rate < 1% for token latency and error budget > 10%).

Discount table (applies to per-token host charges and session warm-capacity add-on; discounts expressed as % off baseline list pricing)

| Median SD (minutes) | Stability signal (percent sessions > threshold) | Discount % | Notes |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------|-------|
| 15 - 29             | >= 70                                           | 7%         | Entry tier for short long sessions |
| 30 - 59             | >= 75                                           | 12%        | Moderate benefit to amortize KV cache |
| 60 - 239            | >= 80                                           | 20%        | High amortization and batching benefits |
| >= 240              | >= 85                                           | 30%        | Exceptional long-lived workloads; review required |

Tiered add-ons and caps

- Maximum discount cap per-account: 40% across all bundled credits and discounts.
- Discounts apply only to hosted per-usage compute line items; reserved/dedicated SKU discounts negotiated separately via Dedicated contracts.
- Discounts are additive with volume credits up to cap; additive rules described in Appendix A.

Contract template language (sales/legal)

Insert the following clause in the commercial SOW or Order Form when enabling duration discounts:

"Duration-Based Consumption Discount. Customer may elect to enroll in Redwood's Duration-Based Consumption Discount Program (\"Program\") for eligible streaming and session workloads. Eligibility will be assessed monthly against the metrics and thresholds defined in Redwood's Stream Duration Discount Framework (internal doc ref). When eligible, Customer will receive the applicable percentage discount to the list price for qualifying compute usage for the upcoming billing cycle. Redwood reserves the right to suspend or modify discount eligibility if the Customer's SLO breach rate exceeds 1% in a trailing 90-day window, or if telemetry indicates sustained unmetered behavior. Details on measurement, dispute resolution, and termination of discounts are provided in Appendix B."

Billing hook implementation (engineering)

The billing system needs a deterministic hook that evaluates eligibility at account-month boundary and applies discount line-item for the next billing period. Pseudocode (for billing scheduler):

```
// Run nightly; evaluate for account A
metrics = fetchSessionMetrics(account = A, window=30d)
median_sd = metrics.median_session_duration_minutes
stability = metrics.percent_sessions_over_threshold(15)
sessions_count = metrics.session_count
slo_breach = fetchSloBreachRate(account = A, window=90d)
if (opt_in && median_sd >= 15 && sessions_count >= 500 && slo_breach < 0.01 && stability >= required) {
  discount_pct = lookupDiscount(median_sd, stability)
  createDiscountLineItem(account=A, percent=discount_pct, effective_from=nextBillingCycle)
} else {
  ensureNoActiveDurationDiscount(account=A)
}
```

Billing schema example (JSON line-item)

```
{
  "account_id": "acct_123",
  "period_start": "2027-06-01",
  "period_end": "2027-07-01",
  "line_items": [
    {
      "sku": "hosted-inference-v4-compute",
      "units": 1234567,
      "unit_price": 0.000012,
      "discounts": [ { "type": "duration", "percent": 0.20, "reason": "median_sd=72" } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Telemetry and metrics requirements

Engineering/telemetry must emit the following signals for each account:

- session_start, session_end, session_id, user_agent, model_variant, kv_cache_hit_rate (per-session), tokens_generated, average_token_latency_ms.
- Derived signals to compute: median_session_duration_minutes, percent_sessions_over_threshold(15m/30m/60m), 30-day rolling session_count, per-account SLO breach rate.

Minimum retention: 90 days for eligibility history; 365 days for audit and dispute resolution. Telemetry must be accessible to billing systems via the internal metrics API (metric names: rw.session.duration_median, rw.session.stability_pct, rw.account.slo_breach_rate).

Anti-gaming and guardrails

To avoid artificial extension of sessions to capture discounts: 

- Sessions that are idle (no tokens generated for > 5 minutes) should be excluded unless explicitly marked as \"interactive still-active\" by the customer through a documented API flag.
- Requests to artificially extend sessions (heartbeat-only traffic) will be flagged if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.1 and token generation rate = 0 for > 80% of the extended window; flagged accounts are suspended from discounts pending review.
- Telemetry anomaly detection must run weekly to detect deviations and surface to customer-success for possible manual review.

Rollout plan (phased)

1) Pilot (Q3 2027) — invite 8 customers (mix of chatbots, contact centers, transcription pipelines) to validate measurement signals, billing hooks, and contract language.
2) Beta (Q4 2027) — open to self-serve opt-in for accounts meeting volume minima with automated billing line-items; limit to 200 accounts for capacity monitoring.
3) GA (Q1 2028) — general availability with UI flags in Console, pricing calculator updates, and public docs.

Operational playbook (CS / Finance / Support)

- Sales: Use the duration discount checkbox on SOW; attach Appendix A additive-credit table if customer negotiates multiple discounts.
- Finance: Verify discount line-item generation for pilot accounts weekly; reconcile with invoices.
- Support/CS: On flagged accounts run the session replay tool and provide remediation or guidance.
- Legal: Use the contract template and escalate any changes to the Program clause.

SLO considerations and risk assessment

- Because discounts are tied to long sessions, we must ensure capacity planning accounts for a higher proportion of sticky connections. Add 12% headroom in warm-pool sizing for accounts on the Program during Beta.
- If long sessions increase KV cache churn, measure per-account cost delta; failure to maintain expected amortization should trigger discount review.

Appendix A — Additive discount decision matrix

- Volume credits (V) + Duration discount (D) apply additively up to cap: Effective discount = min(V + D, account_cap).
- Example: V=10%, D=20%, cap=40% => effective = 30%.

Appendix B — Dispute and audit process (summary)

1) Customer may dispute eligibility within 30 days of invoice.
2) Finance will rerun telemetry calculation for disputed billing cycle within 10 business days.
3) If error found, pro-rated credit is issued and discount eligibility corrected.

Appendix C — Example onboarding checklist for Sales Engineers

- Validate telemetry availability: rw.session.duration_median and rw.account.slo_breach_rate populated for the account.
- Run the session-sample-replay on 3 representative long sessions.
- Estimate cost delta and expected amortization benefit (attach short memo to SOW).
